instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a 'lobbyist' as an individual who receives $2,000 or more in economic consideration in a calendar month (excluding reasonable travel expense reimbursement) to influence legislative or administrative action.

A person (other than a lobbyist employer) must file statements only if it makes payments to influence legislative or administrative action of $5,000 or more in any calendar quarter, implying no filing duty below that threshold.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text defines 'lobbyist' by compensation and job-duty criteria (§ 82039) but does not include any lobbyist-definition expenditure-spending threshold triggering lobbyist registration.

The bundled text contains no quantitative time standard in the definition of 'lobbyist' (only 'principal duties' in § 82039(a)(1) without a measurable magnitude/unit), so a TimeThresholdCell value cannot be derived.

The bundled text requires reporting of 'each activity expense' (§§ 86112, 86114(a)(5), 86116(f)) but contains no per-item dollar de minimis for itemization; if any exists it would be in commission regulations not included here.

The bundled text includes a 10% employee-time threshold for what payments a filer must report (§ 86116(h)(1)) but does not provide a time-percent de minimis exemption from lobbyist registration or from filing lobbyist disclosure.
